title: Circuit Components and Symbols
ques: In a standard electrical circuit diagram, what does a long line next to a shorter, thicker line represent?

answer.content: This symbol represents a **Cell** (or a single battery). The long line represents the positive terminal, and the short thick line represents the negative terminal.

explanation: This teaches standard scientific notation for electrical components.

title: Heating Effect of Current
ques: When you turn on an electric toaster, the wires inside get glowing red and hot. What is this effect of electric current called, and what material is usually used for those wires because it gets hot without melting easily?

answer.content: This is called the **heating effect of electric current**. The material often used is called **Nichrome** wire, because it has a high resistance to electricity, causing it to heat up without melting.

explanation: This explains the operational principle behind common household heating appliances.

title: Magnetic Effect of Current
ques: If you wrap a long copper wire around an iron nail and connect the ends of the wire to a battery, the nail can pick up small metal paperclips. What have you created, and why does this happen?

answer.content: You have created an **electromagnet**. It happens because when electric current flows through the wire, it creates a magnetic field around it, temporarily turning the iron nail into a magnet.

explanation: This demonstrates electromagnetism, a foundational concept linking electricity and magnetism.
